['Uttam Applauds Air Force, Calls for Transparency On Rafale Losses

New Delhi, May 31: Telangana’s Irrigation, Food & Civil Supplies Minister Capt N Uttam Kumar Reddy, a seasoned Indian Air Force veteran, on Saturday demanded full transparency from the Government of India regarding the losses suffered during the recent four-day Indo-Pakistan operation, particularly the reported downing of Rafale fighter jets. 

Addressing a press conference at the AICC headquarters in New Delhi, Uttam Kumar Reddy also pressed the BJP-led Government at the Centre to act urgently on the concerns raised by the Air Force Chief about delays in aircraft supply, talent shortages, and the gap between sanctioned and operational squadrons.

Introducing himself, Uttam Kumar Reddy detailed his own defense background: a graduate of the National Defence Academy, a fully operational fighter pilot who flew MiG-21s on the Chinese border and MiG-23s on the western sector, and a former ADC to the President of India. “I have served at many fighter bases that are now in the news,” he said. “I was a four-aircraft leader and a trainer captain, so I understand the operational realities.” He also highlighted his political career as a six-term MLA and a Member of Parliament, where he served on the Parliamentary Defence Committee alongside Rahul Gandhi, KC Venugopal, and Revanth Reddy.

Uttam Kumar Reddy began by unequivocally praising the Indian Air Force for its role in the recent Indo-Pak operation, describing it as “a very decisive victory.” “All of us in the Congress party are proud of the way the Indian Air Force struck terrorist camps in nine bases across Pakistan and defended our skies with precision,” he said. “It was a truly outstanding operation that met all objectives.”

However, Uttam Kumar Reddy quickly shifted to the serious issues highlighted by Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, who he said had made several statements recently that “should concern all of us.” He cited the Air Chief’s warnings about severe delays in the supply of fighter aircraft and weaponry, which, he said, were “a serious problem for the Air Force.” He also reminded that during his tenure on the Parliamentary Defence Committee, he and his colleagues had repeatedly flagged that India’s operational fighter squadrons were below the sanctioned strength of 42 squadrons - each with 16 to 18 aircraft. “India currently has only 31 squadrons, which is substantially lower than required, especially when we face a collusive threat from both China and Pakistan,” he said.

The minister emphasised that all three armed forces are short of manpower by over 10 percent, an issue worsened by recruitment slowdowns during the COVID-19 pandemic that have yet to recover. “Given the live threats on both our borders, we should be going beyond the sanctioned strength,” he said.

Uttam Kumar Reddy also criticised Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) for failing to deliver the Tejas Mark-1A fighter jets on time, echoing the Air Chief’s frustration. “This can prove to be a serious problem,” he said. “The Air Chief himself expressed his unhappiness about the situation, and the whole country and the Government of India must wake up to the reality that we need to strengthen our armed forces considerably more.”

Quoting the Air Chief Marshal directly, Uttam Kumar Reddy said: “India has fallen behind China in defense technology and production, even as our training standards remain superior.” He stressed that this should be of “serious concern,” urging the government to take necessary corrective steps.

Uttam Kumar Reddy pointed out that the Air Force currently needs 35 to 40 fighter jets annually, but HAL, which is contracted to supply 24 fighter aircraft per year, has failed to deliver even that. “The Air Chief has also flagged a deeper malice - contracts signed with unrealistic deadlines that vitiate the procurement process and erode institutional trust,” he said.

He also addressed the issue of talent shortages in the Air Force, highlighting that the best minds are not joining the service in sufficient numbers, especially in operational and R&D wings. “Technology delayed is technology denied,” he emphasised, calling on the government to attract top talent.

“When Rahul Gandhi ji first raised a question to the External Affairs Minister whether any Rafale has been show down, he was bizarrely accused of being anti-national,” he said. “But today, General Anil Chauhan, the Chief of Defence Staff, has confirmed that Rafale aircraft were brought down.” He also cited Air Marshal Bharti, Director General Air Operations, who in the DGMO briefing said: “Losses are normal in combat. The objectives of the mission have been achieved and all pilots have come home.” Uttam Kumar Reddy emphasised that while the pilots returned safely, “the aircraft have not returned to their bases,” highlighting the need for transparency.

He criticised the BJP government for initially denying these losses and launching a campaign against Rahul Gandhi. “Now that the CDS himself has spoken, the government should stop the denials,” he said. “We are proud of our armed forces, but transparency strengthens trust and helps us learn from every operation.”

Uttam Kumar Reddy also raised questions about the ceasefire announcement during the operation. “How did the US President announce the ceasefire well before the DGMOs of India and Pakistan spoke?” he asked. “The government of India has never clearly explained how this happened.”

He stressed the need for a serious reassessment of India’s defense technology, pointing out that most of the firing during the four-day operation happened from within each country’s international borders. “Yet, we lost fighter aircraft. This requires a thorough review of our technological capabilities,” he said.

['ഗുജറാത്ത് മുതൽ കന്യാകുമാരി വരെയും ബംഗാൾ മുതൽ ലക്ഷദ്വീപ് വരെയുളള തീരപ്രദേശങ്ങളിലെയും ജനങ്ങൾ പ്രകൃതിയുടെ കരുണയിൽ ജീവിതം മുന്നോട്ട് കൊണ്ട് പോകുന്നവരാണ്. നമ്മുടെ രാജ്യത്തിന് അന്നം നല്കുകയും സ്വന്തം കുടുംബങ്ങളിൽ പട്ടിണി അനുഭവിക്കേണ്ടി വരികയും ചെയ്യുന്ന ജനതയാണവർ. ജോലി ചെയ്താലും കൂലിയുറപ്പിലാത്ത ഒരേയൊരു തൊഴിലാണ് മത്സ്യതൊഴിലാളികളുടേത്. 2018 ൽ പ്രളയം കേരളത്തെ വിഴുങ്ങിയപ്പോൾ കേരളത്തിന്റെ സൈന്യമായി പ്രവർത്തിച്ചത് മത്സ്യത്തൊഴിലാളികളായിരുന്നു. പക്ഷേ ഇപ്പോൾ നാം അവരെ വിസ്മരിക്കുകയാണ്. 

കടലിൽ മത്സ്യബന്ധനം നടത്തുന്ന മത്സ്യത്തൊഴിലാളികളെ കൂടാതെ നമ്മുക്ക് കായലിലും പുഴയിലും മത്സ്യബന്ധനം നടത്തുന്ന വലിയൊരു സമൂഹമുണ്ട്. ലോകത്തിലെ തന്നെ ഏറ്റവും വലിയ രണ്ടാമത്തെ മത്സ്യ ഉത്പാദന രാഷ്ട്രമായിരുന്നിട്ട് കൂടി ഈ മേഖലയിലെ സർക്കാർ നയങ്ങൾ ഏറെ തെറ്റായ ദിശയിലൂടെയാണ് സഞ്ചരിക്കുന്നത്. മത്സ്യ മേഖലയുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ട നിരവധി കേന്ദ്ര സർക്കാർ ഡിപ്പാർട്മെന്റുകൾ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നിട്ട് കൂടി മത്സ്യത്തൊഴിലാളികളുടെ സമഗ്ര വിവരങ്ങൾ അടങ്ങുന്ന രേഖകൾ നമ്മുടെ കൈവശമില്ല. നമ്മുടെ തീരദേശങ്ങൾ ലോകത്തിലെ തന്നെ ഏറ്റവും ഉത്പാദനക്ഷമതയുള്ള പ്രദേശങ്ങളാണ്. പക്ഷേ ഇന്ന് അവ തീരശോഷണത്തിന്റെയും, കടൽക്കയറ്റത്തിന്റെയും പിടിയിലാണ്. നമ്മുടെ തീരങ്ങൾ ആരാണ് നിയന്ത്രിക്കുന്നതെന്ന് വെളിപ്പെടുത്താൻ സർക്കാർ ബാധ്യസ്ഥരാണ്. ഇന്ത്യയുടെ വിശാലമായ കടൽത്തീരത്തിന്റെ ഓരോ 500 കിലോമീറ്ററിലും തുറമുഖം സ്ഥാപിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നത് ഒരൊറ്റ കമ്പനി ആണെന്നത് ഒരു അപായസൂചനയാണ്. പശ്ചിമ ബംഗാൾ മുതൽ കേരളത്തിലെ വിഴിഞ്ഞം വരെ അവരുടെ നിയന്ത്രണത്തിലാണ്. തുറമുഖങ്ങളുടെ സ്വകാര്യവത്കരണം മൂലം നിരവധി മത്സ്യതൊഴിലാളികളുടെ വീടുകൾ നഷ്ട്പ്പെടുകയും കുടിയിറക്കപ്പെടുകയും പരമ്പരാഗത തൊഴിൽ ചെയ്യാൻ കഴിയാത്ത സാഹചര്യം ഉണ്ടാവുകയും ചെയ്തു. 

വേമ്പനാട് കായലിൽ പോലും മത്സ്യബന്ധനം സാധ്യമല്ലാത്ത രീതിയിലേക്ക് മാറിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. നമ്മുടെ ജലവിഭവങ്ങൾ വൃത്തിയായി സൂക്ഷിച്ചില്ലെങ്കിൽ അവ ഏറ്റവുമധികം ബാധിക്കുക മത്സ്യത്തൊഴിലാളികളെ ആയിരിക്കും. കടൽ ഖനനവും മത്സ്യത്തൊഴിലാളികളുടെ ജീവിതത്തെ പ്രതിസന്ധിയിലാക്കുന്നു. നമ്മുടെ ശാസ്ത്രജ്ഞർ പറയുന്നത് തീരദേശ കടൽ ഖനനം വലിയ പാരിസ്ഥിതിക പ്രത്യാഘാതം ഉണ്ടാക്കുമെന്നാണ്. ഈ നയത്തിൽ നിന്നും പിന്മാറാൻ സർക്കാർ തയ്യാറാകണം.

["Telangana Budget Is Transformational For Farmers and Welfare  

The Rs. 3.04 lakh crore Telangana's budget for 2025-26, presented by Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Bhatti Vikramarka Mallu  in Assembly on Wednesday, is a bold and progressive financial plan that will strengthen the state’s economy, boost agriculture, and ensure social welfare for all sections of society.  

The allocations made in the budget reflect the government’s commitment to sustainable development, rural empowerment, and food security under the leadership of Chief Minister  Anumula Revanth Reddy . 

Key investments in Irrigation and Civil Supplies will drive long-term growth, benefiting farmers, rural communities, and the economically weaker sections.  

The Rs. 23,373 crore allocation for Irrigation and command area development in the budget prioritises completing pending Irrigation projects and launching new ones, ensuring that Telangana’s farmers receive uninterrupted water supply.  

Further, the Udaya Samudram-Brahmana Velamala Lift Irrigation Project, which will lift 6.70 TMC of water from the Udaya Samudram Balancing Reservoir to the Brahmana Velamala Balancing Reservoir.

The project is designed to Irrigate one lakh acres of land and provide safe drinking water to 107 fluoride-affected villages in Nalgonda and Yadadri Bhuvanagiri districts, bringing much-needed relief to drought-prone areas.  

I welcome the allocation of Rs. 266.65 crore for the revitalisation of the Bunadigani Canal under the Musi Project, which will enhance water distribution for farmers in Yadadri district, ensuring better agricultural output.  

I applaud the Government’s efforts to secure Telangana’s rightful share of Krishna and Godavari river waters. 

The previous administration had failed to act, leading to unfair water allocations favoring Andhra Pradesh. However, under our Congress Government, Telangana has forcefully presented its case before the Brijesh Kumar Tribunal, demanding a fair share of water resources.  

To ensure better management of water resources, I appreciate the government’s plan to implement a real-time telemetry system to monitor water usage that will make the process more transparent and efficient.  

The Rs 5,734 crore allocation for the Civil Supplies Department, will ensure food security for millions of Telangana families.  

The Gruha Jyothi Scheme, which provides free electricity to households consuming up to 200 units has benefited 50 lakh families with this initiative.  The Government allocated Rs 1,775.15 crore to sustain the scheme.  

I welcome the Indiramma Housing Scheme, which provides houses in the name of women beneficiaries. With 4.5 lakh houses sanctioned and Rs 22,500 crore allocated, it is a historic step toward women’s empowerment and housing security.  

Speaking about direct benefits to the poor, the welfare initiatives under the Abhayahastam scheme, including free bus travel for women under the Mahalakshmi scheme, Rs 500 LPG cylinders, and ration card expansions will enhance the quality of life for economically weaker sections.  

The Rs 500 per quintal bonus for fine rice procurement has encouraged an increase in fine rice cultivation from 25 lakh acres to 40 lakh acres. I assure that the state’s paddy procurement system is being strengthened, ensuring farmers get fair prices and are protected from market fluctuations.  

The Rythu Bharosa scheme, under which each farmer will receive Rs 12,000 per acre annually to help cover investment costs for seeds, fertilisers, and technology.  

The Rs. 18,000 crore allocation for the scheme will enhance the financial stability of farmers and boost productivity.  

The Rs. 3.04 lakh crore budget by the Finance Minister has delivered a well-structured plan for inclusive development, ensuring that Telangana progresses toward a trillion-dollar economy.  

The record allocations for marginalised communities including Rs 40,232 crore for Scheduled Caste Welfare; Rs 17,169 crore for Scheduled Tribe Welfare; Rs 11,405 crore for Backward Classes welfare; Rs 31,605 crore for rural development; Rs 12,393 crore for healthcare and Rs 3,591 crore for minority welfare deserves to be appreciated. 

These allocations demonstrate the Government’s commitment to social equity and upliftment.  

This is a budget of hope, progress, and prosperity. It is a budget that prioritizes farmers, strengthens food security, and expands welfare for the underprivileged.

 Under Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s leadership, Telangana is moving towards a brighter, more inclusive future. Every citizen - whether in rural villages or urban centres - will benefit from the vision and policies outlined in this budget."]

  संगमनेर मॉडेल च्या माध्ययमातून मा. थोरातसाहेब यांनी कृषी, शिक्षण, आरोग्य, सहकार विभागात गेली ५O वर्षात अमृतवाहिनी शिक्षण व सहकार उद्योग परिवाराच्या वतीने भरीव कामगिरी करून सामान्य व दुष्काळी भागातील लोकांचे जीवन समृद्ध व संपन्न केले आहे.

  मा. थोरातसाहेब यांची गाठ - भेट व संवाद नेहमीच चेतना व प्रेरणा देणारी ठरत असते. राजकारणी असून देखील, त्यांची आंतरिक वृत्ती तसेच भावना परमानंद प्राप्त व मोहपाशापासून खूपच दूर आहे, असे नेहमीच सर्वांना जाणवते.

['Empowering Young Minds through ‘Shiksha Patra’ - a Team SAI initiative 

Education is the foundation of progress, and digital literacy is the key to unlocking limitless opportunities. As part of Team SAI’s ‘Shiksha Patra’ initiative, we have donated 2 computers to Mandal Parishad Primary School, Yadamma Nagar, ensuring that students have access to modern learning tools.

This initiative is more than just providing computers—it’s about equipping students with essential ICT skills, fostering digital literacy, civic participation, and creating brighter livelihood opportunities. By integrating technology into education, we are bridging the digital divide and empowering the next generation to dream bigger and achieve more.

Every child deserves a future powered by knowledge, and we are committed to making that future a reality.

యువ మేధావులను శిక్షణతో శక్తివంతం చేస్తూ ‘శిక్షా పత్ర’.

విద్య అనేది అభివృద్ధికి పునాది, డిజిటల్ నాలెడ్జ్ అనేది అపరిమిత అవకాశాలను అనలాక్ చేసే తాళం చెవి. ‘శిక్షా పత్ర’ కార్యక్రమంలో భాగంగా మండల్ పరిషత్ ప్రాథమిక పాఠశాల, యాదమ్మ నగర్‌కు 2 కంప్యూటర్లు అందజేయడం జరిగింది, విద్యార్థులకు ఆధునిక విద్యా ఉపకరణాలను అందించే దిశగా మేము మరో ముందడుగు వేశాము.

ఈ కార్యక్రమం కేవలం కంప్యూటర్లను అందజేయడమే కాదు ఇది విద్యార్థులను తరతమమైన ఐసీటీ నైపుణ్యాలతో, డిజిటల్ అక్షరాస్యతను పెంపొందించేందుకు, పౌర జాగ్రత్తలను ప్రోత్సహించేందుకు, మరింత మెరుగైన ఉపాధి అవకాశాలను కల్పించేందుకు ఒక గొప్ప అవకాశాన్ని కల్పిస్తుంది. విద్యను టెక్నాలజీతో సమ్మిళితం చేయడం ద్వారా, డిజిటల్ అంతరాన్ని తగ్గించి, యువతకు మరింత గొప్ప భవిష్యత్తును అందించడమే మా లక్ష్యం.

ప్రతి విద్యార్థికి జ్ఞానం ద్వారా వెలుగొందే భవిష్యత్తు కల్పించాలి అనే ఉద్దేశంతో ముందుకు సాగుతున్నాము.

['நான் பயின்ற கல்லூரி, எனக்கு வழங்கியது “Star of PSGIM“ (ஸ்டார் ஆஃப் பிஎஸ்ஜிஐஎம்) விருது.

அதற்காக நீங்கள் மகிழ்வீர்கள் என்ற சிந்தனையோடும், நன்றி உணர்வோடும் அவ்விருதை பெற்றுக்கொண்டேன்.
—————————————————————
1964-ல் தொடங்கப்பட்ட இந்தக் கல்லூரி, இதுவரை கல்விக்கான தன் 60 ஆண்டுகாலப் பெரும்பயணத்தில், பயின்ற பல்லாயிரக்கணக்கான மாணவர்களில் இதுவரை முப்பது முன்னாள் மாணவர்களுக்கு “Star of PSGIM“ (ஸ்டார் ஆஃப் பிஎஸ்ஜிஐஎம்) என்ற விருதினை கல்லூரி நிர்வாகம் தொடர்ந்து வழங்கிக் கொண்டிருக்கிறது.

அந்தப் புகழ்மிக்க விருதை 01.02.2025 அன்று மாலை கோவை, நீலாம்பூரில் உள்ள PSG convention center அரங்கத்தில் எனக்கு வழங்கி கௌரவித்தது நான் பயின்ற கோவை PSG (பிஎஸ்ஜி) கல்லூரி.

“Star of PSGIM“ (ஸ்டார் ஆஃப் பிஎஸ்ஜிஐஎம்) விருதினைப் பெற்றுக்கொண்டு நன்றி உணர்வோடு நான் பேசிய உரையின் தொகுப்பு:

இந்தக் கல்லூரி எனக்கு கல்விசார் பாடங்களை மட்டுமே கற்றுத் தரவில்லை. என் வாழ்க்கைக்கும், தொழிலுக்கும், இன்றைய என் அரசியல் பணிகளுக்கும் பேருதவியாய் உள்ள பல்வேறு வகையான திறன்களை கற்றுத் தந்துள்ளது. அதில் முக்கியமானதாக, துல்லியமான தொடர்பு திறன், உறவுகளை மேம்படுத்தும் கலை மற்றும் சரியாக முடிவுவெடுக்கும் ஆற்றல் ஆகியவற்றை முதன்மையானதாக நான் இங்கு குறிப்பிட விரும்புகிறேன்.

['गिरिराज जी क्या छुपा रहे है ? किस बात पे पर्दा डाला जा रहा है ?
अपनी विफलता या नीतीश जी की financial bankruptcy या mismanagement, कारण  कुछ भी हो गलती तो NDA की ही है। 
आइए एक एक point की विवेचना की जाए पाते तो चले गिरिराज जी किस criteria की बात कर रहे है। 
PMMITRA यानी प्रधान मंत्री MEGA INTEGRATED TEXTILE REGION & APPAREL कपड़ों उद्योग का industrial cluster है जिसके लिए निम्नलिखित की आवश्यकता है : 
कम से कम 1000 acre का contiguous जमीन का parcel मतलब एक जगह बिना टूटे 1000 एकड़ जमीन, बिहार के पास है, खुद पूर्व उद्योग मंत्री शाहनवाज हुसैन जी ( भाजपाई) ने इसका घोषणा किया था।  ( NEWS CLIP ATTACHED )
Textile and industrial policy : सरकार के लिए ये कोई मुद्दा ही नही। अगर suitable नहीं है तो बनाई जा सकती है , इच्छा शक्ति होनी चाहिए। 
Other textile related facilities PMMITRA के अनुसार ( farm, fibre, factory , fashion, foreign) आइए इसकी गंभीर एवं संक्षिप्त विवेचना करते है। 
कपास की खेती होती थी, बंद हो गई, दोबारा हो तो किसान मालामाल, CASH CROP है कपास। 
कॉटन मिल्स बंद हो गई, खुल जाए  तो रोजगार, ये तो सरकार की TOP PRIORITY होनी चाहिए। 
रेशम अभी भी मिलता है। 
Silk, weaving इत्यादि काफी पहले से होता है। 
Handlooms है। 
Fashion institutes है। 
“जनसंख्या” जो इस उद्योग  के लिए सबसे जरूरी है वो है। 
पहले से छोटे छोटे बहुत से उद्योग है जिन्हें बहुत फायदा मिलता। मुख्य मंत्री रोजगार योजना में कई उद्यमियों को 10 लाख मिला है, मुजफ्फरपुर BIADA के INDUSTRIAL SHED में जगह भी दिया गया था , फिर एक HOWARD EDUCATED बाबू (IAS) को मन किया तो उद्यमियों को बिना कारण agreement का उलंघन करते हुए industrial shed से भगा दिया गया, police से पिटवाया भी , कुछ नेता नेतागीरी किए अब वो उद्यमी भटक रहे है, खैर जस प्रजा तस राजा, VOTERS बिहार में पीटने के लिए ही है। 
फैशन industry में बिहारी बहुतायत में है , किसी भी बड़ा ब्रांड का नीचे से ऊपर हर जगह पर, peon से president तक बिहारी गिरमिटिया मिलेगा। 
अब आते है FOREIGN वाले criteria पे तो माननीय Giriraj जी जो स्थिति बिहार की हैं वहीं UP , तेलंगाना और MP की भी है तो उनका criteria कैसे match कर गया ?
Economies of scale: हमारे यहां हर चीज है जो scale achieve करने के लिए जरूरी है, खास कर के manpower जो इस उद्योग की खास जरूरत है, यही MANPOWER Bangladesh की सफलता का कारण था। 
पानी : यदि आप इस उद्योग से और तिरुपुर के पानी से  परिचित है तो आप जमुई, बांका के पहाड़ी पानी और उसका dyeing उद्योग में उपयोगिता को समझ सकते है, best पानी for dyeing.
 समस्या कहां रह  गई ? गिरिराज जी किस criteria की बात कर रहे है ? कुछ ही कारण दिख रहे है
 या तो नीतीश जी के पास पैसा नहीं है equity participation का 
या हम ये मान ले की बिहारी का गिरमिटिया होना देश के अन्य राज्यों के उद्योगों के लिए जरूरी है ?
या गिरिराज जी की इच्छा नहीं है बिहार में कुछ करने का !!!!!
या केंद्र की priority नहीं है बिहार ?
अब जरा map को ध्यान से देखिए यहां GREENFIELD और BROWNFIELD दो शब्दों का इस्तेमाल हुआ है, जो नहीं समझ पाए उनके लिए साधारण भाषा में , संक्षिप्त में समझा  दूं इन शब्दों का प्रयोग उद्योग और banking sector में बहुत किया जाता है। 
Greenfield मतलब हरी जमीन, जहां अब फावड़ा चलेगा ( spadework ) यानि नींव पड़ेगी मतलब, जिस जमीन पे आज तक कुछ नहीं हुआ है, जहां उद्योग zero से आगे बढ़ेगा। 
Brownfield मतलब जहां पहले से काम हुआ है कुछ, अब उस काम को आगे बढ़ाना है। 
मतलब ये criteria भी नहीं हो सकता PMMITRA पार्क नहीं देने कर, महाराष्ट्र और तेलंगाना को छोड़ दे तो बाकी 5 राज्य में greenfield sanction हुए है, बिहार क्या पाप किया था गिरिराज जी  ?
पाप  voters किया  है नहीं तो 4445 करोड़ तो सिर्फ basic infra cost का रुपया है इसका multiple effect का आप हिसाब भी नहीं लगा सकते वो भी एक कृषि प्रधान बेरोजगार राज्य में।  स्पष्टता के लिए मशहूर गिरिराज जी के मुंह से सच क्यों नहीं निकल रहा ? क्या और किसे छुपा रहे है ?

Unmasking Resistance to India's Progress
 ******************************************
 
In the realm of politics, when transformative changes are introduced, it is not uncommon for a certain section of politicians to resist and criticize them. The Narendra Modi-led government in India has been a catalyst for significant reforms and development. However, as their hold on the country's politics is slipping away, some political factions, including Congress and break India forces, are resorting to labelling these changes as dictatorial rule or anarchy. Today we will delve into the underlying dynamics and motivations behind such accusations.
 
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Indian government has embarked on a path of ambitious reforms aimed at propelling the nation's growth on both domestic and global fronts. Initiatives such as Digital India, Make in India, and Swachh Bharat Abhiyan have sought to address long-standing challenges, foster innovation, and enhance India's global standing. As a result, India's economic growth has surged, foreign direct investment has increased, and the nation's technological prowess has garnered international recognition.
 
With the Modi government's progressive policies yielding positive outcomes, certain factions of the political spectrum are finding their grip on power slipping away. This has led to resistance and attempts to undermine the government's achievements by branding them as dictatorial rule or anarchy. The accusations serve as a rhetorical weapon, attempting to delegitimize the transformative changes taking place and instigate public doubt.
 
 
Congress, India's prominent political party, which once held power for several decades, finds itself at a crossroads. The emergence of the Modi government and its resounding mandate from the people have posed a challenge to Congress' traditional dominance. Faced with the reality of diminishing support, some members of Congress have resorted to labelling the government's reforms as dictatorial.
 
Similarly, break India forces, comprising separatist groups and individuals advocating for the disintegration of the nation also feel threatened by the progress achieved under the Modi government. ନୂଆଦିଲ୍ଲୀର ପ୍ରଗତି ମଇଦାନରେ ଚାଲିଛି ଭାରତ ଅନ୍ତର୍ଜାତୀୟ ବାଣିଜ୍ୟ ମେଳା ୨୦୨୪। ଏହି ବିଶାଳ ବାଣିଜ୍ୟ ମେଳାର ପ୍ରମୁଖ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ପାଲଟିଛି ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ର ‘ଓଡ଼ିଶା ମଣ୍ଡପ’। ‘ବିକଶିତ ଭାରତ ବିକଶିତ ଓଡ଼ିଶା’ ଥିମରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ହୋଇଛି ଓଡ଼ିଶା ମଣ୍ଡପର ଡିଜାଇନ। ମେଳାରେ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ସାଜିଛି ରାଜ୍ୟ ସରକାରଙ୍କ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ବିଭାଗ ପକ୍ଷରୁ ଖୋଲାଯାଇଥିବା ୨୫ଟି ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ର ଷ୍ଟଲ୍। ଏଥିରେ ଓଡ଼ିଶାର କଳା କାରିଗରି, ହସ୍ତତନ୍ତ, ହସ୍ତଶିଳ୍ପ ସାମଗ୍ରୀ ସହିତ ଜନଜାତି ସଂସ୍କୃତି ଓ କଳାକୃତି ସ୍ଥାନ ପାଇଛି। ହସ୍ତତନ୍ତ ଓ ହସ୍ତଶିଳ୍ପ ସାମଗ୍ରୀ ସହିତ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ ଉତ୍ପାଦ କିଣିବାକୁ ଭିଡ଼ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ମିଳୁଛି। ‘ଓଡ଼ିଶା ମଣ୍ଡପ’ର ଆଉ ଏକ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ହେଉଛି ରାଜ୍ୟର ଅନନ୍ୟ ହସ୍ତକଳା ଓ ହସ୍ତଶିଳ୍ପ ସାମଗ୍ରୀର ଲାଇଭ୍ ଡେମନଷ୍ଟ୍ରେସନ। ଏଠାରେ ଓଡ଼ିଶାର କାରିଗରମାନେ ପଟ୍ଟଚିତ୍ର, ରୁପା ତାରକସି ଓ ସବାଇ ଘାସରୁ ବିଭିନ୍ନ ଉତ୍ପାଦ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅହିଂସା ଉପାୟରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ‘କରୁଣା ସିଲ୍କ’ ଦେଶ ବିଦେଶର ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଆକର୍ଷିତ କରୁଛି।

['Rising Pollution in Delhi-NCR: Real Estate Sector Voices Concerns and Proposes Solutions

Construction Activities Halted in Delhi-NCR In response to rising pollution levels in Delhi-NCR, the government has enforced Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). This includes a ban on construction activities and restrictions on vehicular movement. While the step aims to control pollution, it has raised serious concerns within the real estate industry. The Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI) has shared its perspective and offered recommendations to tackle the issue effectively.

As one of the largest employers of unskilled labor, the real estate sector faces significant challenges with these restrictions. Thousands of workers’ livelihoods are at stake, and ongoing projects are at risk of delays, impacting delivery timelines and budgets.

CREDAI’s Suggestion: Exempt RERA-Compliant Projects Manoj Gaur, President of CREDAI NCR and CMD of Gaur Group, emphasized the importance of balancing pollution control measures with the needs of the real estate industry. He stated:

Controlling pollution is essential, but halting all construction activities is not the right solution. It directly affects workers’ livelihoods and delays projects, especially those adhering to RERA’s stringent timelines. We urge the government to exempt RERA-approved projects under GRAP so that development continues without disrupting economic stability.

Gaur highlighted that delays caused by construction bans disrupt project budgets and timelines, leading to penalties under RERA guidelines. Thousands of homebuyers are already waiting for their homes, and such restrictions could further delay their possession.

Developers’ Role: Steps to Minimize Pollution Amit Modi, Director of County Group, supported GRAP’s implementation but suggested a pragmatic approach for the real estate sector:

It’s crucial to reduce pollution in Delhi-NCR, and the construction sector must play its part. Developers should prioritize non-polluting activities at sites, such as interior work, pipe fittings, flooring, aluminum and glass installations, wiring, sanitary fittings, and landscaping. This ensures timely project completion while minimizing environmental harm.

Modi stressed that developers must adopt eco-friendly practices to contribute to pollution control during this challenging period.

Balancing Environment and Development: Harsh Gupta’s Recommendations Harsh Gupta, CEO of Sundream Group, proposed strategies to strike a balance between environmental concerns and development. He stated:

Instead of a blanket ban on construction activities, pollution-intensive tasks like material transportation and mixing should be suspended. However, interior work, painting, and fittings can continue, ensuring that projects stay on track and workers’ livelihoods remain intact.

Technology-Driven Solutions: Ansal Housing’s Approach Kushagra Ansal, Director of Ansal Housing, emphasized the need for modern technology to address pollution concerns. He said:

Pre-cast construction techniques and dust control equipment should be adopted. These methods not only mitigate environmental impact but also ensure timely completion of projects. We also recommend the government introduce specific guidelines for RERA-approved projects to maintain a balance between environmental conservation and the real estate sector’s growth.

A Call for Practical Solutions The real estate industry acknowledges the urgency of addressing pollution in Delhi-NCR. However, a balanced approach is essential to avoid disruption in development activities and safeguard the livelihoods of thousands of workers.

Exempting RERA-compliant projects from construction bans, adopting environmentally friendly technologies, and implementing targeted restrictions are practical solutions that can ensure progress while maintaining environmental harmony. Collaboration between the government and developers is key to achieving these objectives and addressing the dual challenges of pollution control and economic stability.

['Why Are Noida’s Malls Failing? Exploring the Decline of Retail in the City

Noida’s Retail Woes
Once a hub of shopping and entertainment, Noida’s retail sector is facing an unprecedented slowdown. From dwindling footfall to high vacancy rates, the city’s malls are struggling to stay afloat. The recent sale of Logix City Centre Mall is a glaring example of the challenges plaguing the industry. This article dives into the reasons behind this decline and what lies ahead for Noida’s retail sector.

The Logix Mall Sale: A Telling Example
Logix City Centre Mall, located in Sector 32, was recently acquired by the Bhutani Group for approximately ₹1,000 crore. Once bustling with nearly 10,000 daily visitors, the mall’s footfall plummeted to less than 2,000 in the past five years. The Bhutani Group plans to redevelop the property, aiming to restore its former glory. However, the question remains—can redevelopment alone revive the fortunes of Noida’s struggling retail spaces?

A Broader Decline Across Noida’s Retail Sector
The challenges faced by Logix Mall are not unique. Prominent shopping destinations like The Great India Place, DLF Mall of India, and Gardens Galleria are also grappling with similar issues:

Vacant Spaces:

The Great India Place has 30% of its retail space unoccupied.

Vacancies in other malls across Noida have increased by 20-40% over the past five years.

Footfall Crisis:

Foot traffic in malls has dropped by 30% in the last half-decade.

Retailers face mounting losses, with rising rents and maintenance costs further exacerbating the situation.

Why Are Noida’s Malls Struggling?
Several factors have contributed to the downfall of Noida’s once-thriving retail sector:

Rise of E-Commerce:
Online shopping has reshaped consumer habits, drawing customers away from physical stores. The convenience and variety offered by e-commerce giants have made malls less attractive.
High Operational Costs:
Steep rental rates and maintenance expenses have created significant challenges for retailers, making profitability increasingly difficult.
Can Redevelopment Revive Noida’s Retail Spaces?
Despite the gloom, developers like Bhutani Group remain optimistic. Following the Logix Mall acquisition, the company claims that all remaining retail units were sold within hours. The focus is now on introducing innovative concepts such as:

Interactive Shopping Experiences: Enhancing customer engagement through technology.

Family-Centric Entertainment: Offering attractions beyond shopping.

While these measures could attract new visitors, their success in reversing the overall decline remains uncertain.

The Road Ahead: Is There Hope for Noida’s Retail Sector?
The struggles of Noida’s malls highlight broader challenges in India’s retail landscape. Developers are exploring creative solutions, but the competition from e-commerce and changing consumer preferences pose significant hurdles.

Investors and retailers must adapt to this evolving market, leveraging innovation and technology to stay relevant. Whether Noida’s malls can reinvent themselves as thriving commercial hubs or fade into obscurity will depend on their ability to meet these challenges head-on.

Noida’s retail sector is at a crossroads. As malls like Logix undergo transformation, the city’s shoppers and investors are left wondering: will these spaces once again become the bustling hubs they once were? The answer may determine the future of retail in Noida.

New Report Projects 33.89 Million Job Growth Driven by AI and Tech Transformation

India’s labor market is on a transformative path, with the workforce projected to expand from 423.7 million in 2023 to 457.6 million by 2028, a net increase of 33.89 million jobs. This insight comes from a new report by American software firm ServiceNow, which highlights the potential of emerging technologies to reshape talent across key sectors and generate 2.73 million new positions in tech alone over the next five years.

Key Findings of the Report: Tech, Manufacturing, Education, and Healthcare on the Rise

The report outlines substantial job creation across several industries due to anticipated economic growth and advancements in technology:

Technology Sector: 2.73 million new jobs by 2028, driven by demand for roles in areas like software application development and data engineering.

Manufacturing: Expected to generate 1.5 million jobs, as innovation reshapes production and processes.

Education: Projected to add 84,000 jobs, fueled by a push toward digital learning solutions and online education.

Healthcare: An estimated 80,000 new positions, supported by increasing investment in digital health services.

This surge in demand is presenting professionals, especially those in retail, with valuable opportunities to upskill in tech-centric roles, the report noted.

AI as a Catalyst for Job Creation in India

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a crucial driver of employment growth across India’s leading sectors. According to ServiceNow India Technology and Business Center's Senior Vice President and Managing Director, Sumeet Mathur, AI will be instrumental in creating jobs that require advanced technical expertise. “This strategic emphasis on AI will not only provide high-value opportunities for professionals but also enable them to build sustainable digital careers,” Mathur stated.

He emphasized that by equipping the workforce with advanced tech skills, India can maintain its competitive edge in the global technology landscape.

Role-Specific Impact: How AI Will Revolutionize the Workforce

The report offers an in-depth look at how specific roles will benefit from the integration of AI and other advanced technologies:

AI Systems Engineers: Expected to see significant growth, with Generative AI contributing to half of the total tech impact in this role.

Implementation Consultants: Could save up to 1.9 hours per week by automating repetitive tasks, freeing time for more strategic projects.

Platform Owners: The least impacted, yet anticipated to save nearly half an hour each week as AI streamlines routine operations.

Emerging technologies are set to transform the tech ecosystem, enabling professionals to work smarter and more efficiently across the board, the report concluded.

A Data-Driven Forecast: Ensuring India’s Leadership in the Global Tech Economy

This report’s projections are based on a comprehensive analysis of India’s labor market using census and labor force data, alongside economic growth forecasts from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). By fostering tech skills in its workforce, India can secure a leading role in the global digital economy.

As India’s job market continues to expand, the influence of AI and other technologies offers both opportunities and challenges, positioning the country for a tech-driven future powered by a skilled and adaptable workforce.

['"Job Market Boom to Fuel Real Estate Demand: Rising High-Paying Jobs Set to Drive Housing Growth in India"

Rising employment opportunities in India are set to provide a significant boost to the real estate sector, as an expanding job market—especially in high-paying tech and advanced sectors—fuels a demand surge for housing. According to a recent report by ServiceNow, India's workforce is expected to grow by 33.89 million by 2028, with emerging technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation creating millions of jobs in tech, manufacturing, education, and healthcare. This uptick in employment is anticipated to have a ripple effect on the real estate sector, as increased job opportunities and incomes create a heightened demand for residential properties.

The Connection Between Job Growth and Real Estate Demand

Historically, employment growth has had a strong correlation with housing demand. As more individuals secure jobs, particularly high-paying roles in tech and skilled industries, they look to invest in housing. Cities with a strong job market and high salaries often see a corresponding rise in demand for real estate, especially in urban areas and emerging residential zones.

With the rapid growth in sectors like technology, manufacturing, and healthcare, India’s middle and upper-middle classes are expected to expand, generating a broader customer base for both affordable and luxury housing markets. Tech hubs like Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and emerging metro regions are already seeing a steady increase in property prices and rental demand due to high-paying tech jobs, and this trend is likely to accelerate in the coming years.

Tech Industry as a Major Housing Demand Driver

The ServiceNow report anticipates that the technology sector alone will generate 2.73 million jobs by 2028. Many of these roles—such as software application developers, AI systems engineers, and data specialists—are in high demand and offer substantial compensation. As these employees settle into stable, well-paid careers, they often look to secure their financial future through property investments, spurring demand in both rental and ownership markets.

Moreover, the influx of tech talent in certain cities fosters development of lifestyle amenities, premium housing projects, and luxury living spaces to cater to the tastes of highly-skilled professionals. As the tech industry continues to grow, it will drive residential demand in both city centers and suburban areas close to tech parks and business hubs.

Other Sectors Contributing to Housing Growth

Beyond technology, job creation in manufacturing, healthcare, and education is also poised to stimulate real estate growth. Manufacturing is expected to generate 1.5 million new jobs by 2028, creating demand for housing near industrial areas and logistical hubs. Meanwhile, the healthcare sector, with 80,000 projected new jobs, and education, with 84,000, will require residential infrastructure as professionals look for housing in urban centers and surrounding areas with good connectivity.

As these sectors expand, the need for residential projects catering to mid- to high-income professionals will rise, encouraging developers to invest in quality housing solutions. Additionally, the growth of the service sector has spurred the development of retail, entertainment, and leisure facilities, further enhancing the value of real estate in these areas.

Urbanization and the Move Toward Smart Cities

With rising employment opportunities, India's ongoing urbanization will also intensify, as people migrate to metropolitan and Tier-2 cities in search of better career prospects. This urban migration will continue to boost demand for housing in urban centers, prompting developers to construct new residential projects, including affordable housing and modern apartments with smart city features.

The government’s Smart Cities Mission aligns well with this trend, as cities are now being designed with improved infrastructure, connectivity, and sustainability. This effort to modernize cities in line with global standards makes these regions more attractive for housing investment, both for individual homeowners and real estate investors looking for long-term returns.

Real Estate Growth Driven by Rising Incomes

The growth of high-paying job opportunities, particularly in tech, is resulting in a substantial increase in disposable income for many Indian households. This growth in income levels is a powerful catalyst for real estate investment, as more professionals seek not only primary residences but also investment properties.

The rise in housing demand could lead to a steady appreciation in property prices, particularly in cities where tech and other high-growth sectors are concentrated. Additionally, the preference for homeownership over renting is growing among young professionals, as the financial benefits of owning property align well with long-term wealth-building goals.

A Positive Outlook for Real Estate

India’s projected job growth across key industries is set to act as a “booster dose” for the real estate market, as rising incomes and an influx of well-paid professionals drive housing demand. By creating new economic opportunities, the rapid expansion of the job market is reinforcing the appeal of property investments, making real estate a lucrative sector poised for sustainable growth.

With employment and income levels on the rise, India's real estate market is primed to enter a new era of expansion, catering to a diverse demographic of buyers and investors seeking to benefit from a dynamic and evolving economy.

Labor Costs Push Construction Expenses Higher as Key Material Prices Stabilize

Gurugram, 14 November 2024 — The average cost of construction has surged up to 11% over the past year across India’s real estate sectors, mainly driven by rising labor expenses and a moderate increase in the cost of essential materials like sand, bricks, glass, and wood. Despite some stability in the prices of key materials such as steel and aluminum, labor costs have spiked by approximately 25% year-on-year in the private sector, intensifying financial pressures on developers.

Labor Costs Outweigh Material Costs in Construction Budgets

In the past 12 months, key construction materials have seen modest price movements, with cement prices notably declining by 15% and steel prices dropping slightly by 1%. However, labor costs have escalated sharply, making up over one-fourth of the overall construction budget. This surge reflects the rising demand for skilled labor, along with costs associated with training, safety, and regulatory compliance.

Badal Yagnik, CEO of Colliers India, noted, “Labor costs are driving up construction expenses significantly. With a 25% rise in labor costs, project budgets are increasingly stretched, which in turn impacts operational costs. Skilled labor demand and compliance costs are adding to this financial strain.”

Source: Colliers India

Residential Sector Faces the Highest Construction Cost Increase

The residential sector has experienced the most significant cost increases, with a year-on-year rise of around 11% as of October 2024. The growing demand for gated communities and quality infrastructure has driven residential developers to improve their offerings, which has contributed to higher construction expenses.

Source: Colliers India

Market Resilience Despite Rising Costs

Despite escalating costs, both the commercial and industrial real estate markets have witnessed robust supply additions in 2024. The office market, for example, recorded 37 million square feet of new completions in the first nine months of 2024, while the industrial and warehousing sectors saw 22 million square feet of fresh supply. Developers are increasingly adopting technology and sustainability practices across asset classes to meet the ongoing demand for Grade A developments.

Vimal Nadar, Senior Director and Head of Research at Colliers India, observed, “The commercial and industrial sectors continue to see strong new supply, and project schedules remain largely on track. Developers are advancing technology and sustainability measures to offset rising costs and enhance operational efficiency.”

Developers Turn to Cost Optimization and Local Sourcing

To address construction cost pressures, developers are revising budgets, improving supply chain management, and sourcing materials locally. Investments in automation and workforce training are also helping developers tackle skilled labor shortages, potentially easing project scheduling challenges.

In the long term, developers are expected to focus on circular economy principles, which promote resource efficiency and cost savings. By incorporating sustainable practices, developers can not only reduce costs but also enhance construction efficiency, fostering a more resilient and eco-friendly real estate landscape.
